findings: Latest Kaiju interaction-ownership scar is repaired in policy source: persistent selection no longer automatically outranks newer direct keyboard focus.
Code-first review found and repaired a secondary evidence-loss bug: capture-time keyboard-focus identity remains evidence even if that secondary control disappears from the accepted current model.
The backward-compatible service-consumed overload now fails closed when heartbeat-child focus is empty, preventing missing focus-scope evidence from being treated as rebuild evidence.
The explicit overload preserves touch-selected behavior only when complete scope evidence proves no newer direct focus, and grants captured-focus loss amnesty only for a focus-destroying mutation.
A hostile standalone regression source covers newer keyboard focus superseding persistent selection, removed captured-focus baseline, and explicit no-focus scope.

The existing OperatorOverlayService still calls the backward-compatible overload and still does not provide actual mutation class plus overlay-wide direct-focus presence. Existing-owner explicit focus-scope wiring therefore remains NO.
The ready-to-apply OperatorOverlayService patch is durable proposal evidence only; it is not implemented service wiring.
TalkBack accessibility focus remains deliberately unqueried and unproven; direct keyboard focus must not be promoted to TalkBack focus evidence.
